segments.text: This episode is about parents learning when to take charge and when to step back.

segments.text: Luke and Manny play on the same basketball team, but their coach spends most of the game yelling at the children and calling them names. Phil tries to speak to him calmly, but Jay steps in and threatens him. The coach gets angry, quits on the spot, and tells Jay to take over.
segments.tts_text: [a natural conversational storyteller] Luke and Manny play on the same basketball team, but their coach spends most of the game yelling at the children and calling them names. Phil tries to speak to him calmly, but Jay steps in and threatens him. The coach gets angry, quits on the spot, and tells Jay to take over.

segments.text: Phil has coached basketball before and thinks he should get the job. Jay ignores him, makes himself head coach, and treats Phil like an assistant. He tells the boys to play aggressively, but the team only gets worse. Phil keeps offering useful advice, while Jay refuses to listen.

segments.text: Phil finally tells Jay that he’s tired of being pushed aside. It isn’t only about basketball. Earlier, Jay also took over the grill at a family barbecue because he didn’t trust Phil to cook the steaks properly.

segments.text: Jay admits that he likes being in control and should’ve let Phil coach from the beginning.

segments.text: Phil takes over near the end of the game. He creates a simple play that gives Manny a chance to take his first shot of the season. Manny almost scores, and even though the team still loses, the boys finally start playing together.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Claire takes Alex shopping, but Alex is embarrassed when they run into some girls from school. She asks Claire to wait in the car and acts as if being seen with her mother is the worst thing in the world.

segments.text: At the basketball game, Gloria has the same problem. She cheers so loudly for Manny that the other children make fun of him. Manny asks her not to come to the next game. Both mothers are hurt because their children suddenly seem to want less of them.

segments.text: Claire later gets her revenge when Alex asks for money to go out with her friends. She gives Alex the money, then loudly talks to her like a little girl in front of everyone. Gloria takes a different approach.

segments.text: She talks so much about the lovely day she had with Lily that Manny becomes jealous and invites her to his next game.

segments.text: Mitchell is still out of work, while Cameron has taken a part-time job. Mitchell says he enjoys staying home with Lily, and Cameron says he enjoys working, but neither of them is being honest.

segments.text: Jay introduces Mitchell to a successful businessman who offers him a job. Cameron makes the meeting awkward by talking too much, but the two of them finally admit what they really want: Mitchell misses working, and Cameron misses staying home with Lily.

segments.text: As they’re leaving, they accidentally lock themselves in the garage. While trying to get out, they press the wrong controls and repeatedly crash their car into the man’s Ferrari. Mitchell accepts the job, partly because he now has a very expensive accident to make up for.

segments.text: By the end, Phil gets his chance to lead, Mitchell returns to work, and the mothers realize that their children still need them, even when they don’t always want to show it.
